posts.title: The Digital Paradigm and AI: A Perspective
posts.description: A perspective on AI as productivity acceleration, changing skill models, and the future of work in the current digital paradigm.

posts.contentHtml:
AI isn’t replacing us until we are stuck in world’s current digital paradigm.

Since I started using a PC, it has evolved mainly in screen sizes, but the interface remains similar. Click sounds and voice inputs have changed, but the core input controls are almost the same. Storage hasn’t fundamentally changed; it’s just moved to another city or server where there’s less chaos. Computation is still based on 0s and 1s.

Roles have evolved, and the speed of work has increased dramatically, from 2x to 10x. The digital era itself has evolved, but people’s perspectives remain largely unchanged, keeping us stuck in the same paradigm.

AI advancements in this digital era are still constrained by connectivity, infrastructure like storage and processing, and classical computing’s binary foundation.

I can safely say AI is not a paradigm shift.

But this speed comes at a cost. Our attention spans are limited, and we may need a paradigm shift to fully embrace the evolution of the digital paradigm. Or perhaps we’re silently heading toward a new paradigm already. In the current paradigm, however, our attention spans struggle to process the overwhelming amount of information, which can lead to burnout.

That’s why I see AI differently. I have assumed for clarity of mind that AI is not replacing us but rather boosting our productivity. People and industries that have vanished aren’t being replaced by AI; they’re being outpaced by those who have adapted and increased their productivity. It’s a simple game of supply and demand: the demand for quality products will be met by top-quality suppliers. The demand for lower-quality products will persist as well.

This game’s changing how we grow. In this paradigm, scaling horizontally feels more feasible than scaling vertically. People, including myself, are more focused on broadening their skill sets.

Take my profession: these roles were a complete team or departments, Marketing and Sales representative, Front end engineer, Backend ednginer, QA, Manager, Product owner. Now it will gradually start merging not by design but by choice or may be expectations evolved and there would be no choice, people will start scaling them horizontally and eventually in other areas as well roles like polymath and soloprenuers will emerge.

More skills mean more challenges. As opportunities grow, challenges will grow alongside them.

Soft skills will become more important than ever. English, or another widely spoken language, may become the primary medium for interaction and exchanging ideas.

Simply having thoughts won’t be enough; articulating those thoughts into words will be critical.

Content creation will no longer be just a profession but a survival skill, much like cooking.

People will grow bored with AI-generated content and crave authentic interaction, real voices, real expressions.

Mental health issues will cease to be a taboo topic; people will discuss them openly because there will be no other choice.

posts.title: Sometimes the Anxiety You Feel Isn’t About the Moment: It’s Your Younger Self Asking to Be Seen, Heard, and Healed
posts.description: A reflective article on hidden anxiety, subconscious triggers, and mindful self-observation for emotional healing.
posts.excerpt: Sometimes we observe hidden anxiety, with the conscious mind unaware of it. When anxiety hits, it doesn't only affect emotional behavior but also reflects in cognitive...
posts.contentHtml:
Sometimes we observe hidden anxiety, with the conscious mind unaware of it. When anxiety hits, it doesn't only affect emotional behavior but also reflects in cognitive behaviors and physical symptoms. Sometimes it's due to an obvious reason at work i.e. someone is not respecting your red lines, and your belief about protecting those boundaries, along with your inability to express yourself, causes the anxiousness within you. Or you encounter a seller not fulfilling a contracted obligation, which contradicts your belief in receiving quality service in exchange for money, and you become defensive and try to protect your money. These situations heighten your body's fight-or-flight responses, and you quickly regain control.

Sometimes you aren't aware of the obvious reason, but behind the scenes, your subconscious perceives a threat to your belief system. You're working extra hours or consistently on weekends and enjoying the work, unintentionally going beyond the limit. But the belief or the intensity of the belief stored in your subconscious mind about working hours or weekends contradicts that. You were enjoying the work, but the body unconsciously perceived it as a threat and activated the fight-or-flight response due to the contradiction with that belief.

This intensity of belief could stem from hidden or unprocessed trauma, which is still not visible to the conscious mind but remains in the subconscious. I usually listen to bodily symptoms along with cognitive behavior and avoid reacting impulsively. I step back, journal the thoughts, and look for patterns and reasoning in daily activities. Sometimes the cause becomes visible, but other times I postpone it, knowing that unprocessed desires won’t just fade away they will eventually find a way to surface if pursued mindfully.

Keep an eye on physical symptoms and your cognitive behavior if something seems unusual, it might be a sign of hidden anxiety.

Hidden anxiety is often a blend of past pain and future fear… stored quietly in the nervous system.

Unresolved trauma may be seeking attention, don’t ignore it. It might be your younger self asking for help.

featuredProjects.title: Data Landscape Scanner
featuredProjects.summary: A data discovery and governance system supporting 40+ technologies for cataloguing, lineage, and classification.
featuredProjects.description: The Data Landscape Scanner project revolutionizes data discovery and governance by supporting over 40 technologies, including Oracle, Snowflake, AWS Glue, and Tableau.
featuredProjects.role: Worked across connectors, security hardening, metadata discovery, and scanner optimization.

blocks.content: Enterprise teams needed one dependable way to discover, classify, and trace data assets across databases, warehouses, BI tools, and cloud platforms. Coverage gaps and inconsistent metadata discovery made governance harder as the ecosystem expanded.

items: Data assets lived across a wide mix of technologies.
Metadata discovery quality varied from connector to connector.
Security concerns around scanner-side query behavior increased operational risk.

sections.title: How the scanner became more useful

blocks.content: The platform was expanded to support broader technology coverage, stronger metadata discovery, and safer execution patterns. The work focused on making cataloguing and lineage dependable enough for real enterprise adoption.

blocks.caption: Coverage and discovery work centered on making metadata collection broader, more accurate, and safer across enterprise systems.

blocks.content: My contribution spanned connector delivery, scanner hardening, and metadata improvement work across multiple technologies.

items: Built and improved connectors for systems including dbt, Kafka, and Power BI.
Mitigated SQL injection risks and tightened scanner-side query safety.
Implemented tag discovery for database objects to improve classification workflows.
Optimized scanner behavior for Azure Synapse, Databricks, and Snowflake.
Expanded discovery coverage across a broader set of enterprise technologies.
Improved governance readiness with stronger classification and tagging support.
Reduced operational risk by hardening query execution and connector behavior.
Made lineage and cataloguing more dependable for large heterogeneous estates.

featuredProjects.seoDescription: The Data Landscape Scanner project revolutionizes data discovery and governance by supporting over 40 technologies, including Oracle, Snowflake, AWS Glue, and Tableau.

featuredProjects.title: Unified Data Platform (UDP)
featuredProjects.summary: A platform for designing and deploying big data pipelines without exposing users to infrastructure complexity.
featuredProjects.description: UDP gives data teams a way to design and deploy ETL workflows without carrying the full burden of orchestration and infrastructure complexity.
featuredProjects.role: Built backend platform capabilities, Airflow integrations, quality controls, and automated testing coverage.

blocks.content: Data teams needed to create and deploy ETL pipelines quickly without being slowed down by orchestration detail, infrastructure friction, or weak visibility into runtime behavior.

items: Pipeline builders needed a simpler operating model.
Execution visibility had to be stronger for production diagnosis.
Engineering quality needed to improve across multiple repositories at once.

blocks.content: Core backend capabilities were built to make pipeline creation, orchestration insight, and platform operations more dependable. The work combined product delivery with quality improvements so the platform became easier to trust in production.

blocks.caption: The platform work focused on making data-pipeline delivery simpler for users while making execution and quality signals clearer for the engineering teams behind it.

blocks.content: I worked across platform features, orchestration integrations, reliability, and engineering-quality improvements while still meeting active sprint and production commitments.

items: Designed and implemented backend features for ETL and notebook-related workflows.
Integrated Airflow visibility to expose deeper insight into job and pipeline execution.
Resolved production issues within strict SLAs while keeping sprint delivery on track.
Automated complex end-to-end ETL testing and introduced SonarQube quality controls.
Improved platform reliability and day-to-day delivery confidence for data teams.
Reduced manual validation effort through stronger automated coverage.
Raised code quality and coverage across repositories while addressing critical issues.
Lowered security and maintenance risk through better CI and code-health discipline.

featuredProjects.seoDescription: UDP gives data teams a way to design and deploy ETL workflows without carrying the full burden of orchestration and infrastructure complexity.

featuredProjects.title: Error Reprocessing Tool
featuredProjects.summary: A system for monitoring and recovering data migration failures in near real time.
featuredProjects.description: ERT gave data and cloud teams a focused platform for tracking, analyzing, and reprocessing failures during on-prem to Azure migration work.
featuredProjects.role: Helped improve observability, recovery workflows, and operational reliability during migration work.

sections.title: The migration risk that had to be reduced

blocks.content: Migration work moved quickly, but failure handling could not remain vague. Teams needed a reliable way to identify errors, understand what went wrong, and recover without slowing delivery momentum.

items: Errors had to be surfaced close to real time.
Recovery paths needed to support both automated and operator-led actions.
Observability had to become clearer for engineering teams working under migration pressure.

blocks.content: The platform centralized error visibility and supported structured reprocessing workflows so failures could be diagnosed and recovered more confidently during migration activity.

blocks.caption: The tool was designed around fast visibility into migration failures and clearer recovery paths when issues surfaced in live movement workflows.

blocks.content: I contributed to the monitoring and recovery experience with a focus on making the workflow more usable and operationally dependable for teams responding to migration failures.

items: Supported monitoring and analysis flows for migration-related failures.
Improved recovery behavior for both automated and operator-driven reprocessing.
Contributed to overall platform reliability for near real-time operational use.
Helped shape a workflow that reduced friction for engineering teams handling migration incidents.
Improved observability for migration failures in near real time.
Reduced recovery friction through clearer reprocessing paths.
Lowered migration delivery risk with more dependable operational tooling.
Made error handling more structured for cloud migration teams.

featuredProjects.seoDescription: ERT gave data and cloud teams a focused platform for tracking, analyzing, and reprocessing failures during on-prem to Azure migration work.
